item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Being old, this has lots of tone "issues" by modern standards, but some of those new standards? I don't care what current consensus on The Administrator is, that line about it getting dusty is hilarious! One does bug me though — the end of the first test this happens:

Subject-722M's wounds are treated, and his condition is inconsequential.

That second clause is cold even by Foundation standards. Can it be "is considered inconsequential" or "is inconsequential to this test/research/etc"? It's that minor difference between "he might've died, but so what?" and "if he died, it's not relevant to the matter at hand", and it's bugging me.

In other things, I want that coat. Not the skip, that actual coat. Because even without the extra arms, that's a nice coat; the extra arms are icing.

I'm genuinely shocked this is rated as highly as it is, even by series 1 standards.

Despite getting a big laugh from this:

SCP-262 is placed on an anatomically-correct human male mannequin dressed in typical SCP personnel attire. After several minutes, a single human arm emanating from the inner lining of SCP-262 reaches up towards the mannequin's face. After several prods of apparent curiosity, the arm retreats and no further movement is recorded for the duration of the test.

I don't particularly like the idea enough to vote it up
